✈️ Why did Jet Airways — once India’s most premium airline — suddenly collapse?

For years, Jet Airways wasn’t just another airline. It represented the golden era of Indian aviation. Known for its five-star service, punctual flights, iconic yellow-jacket cabin crew, and premium in-flight experience, Jet Airways became the preferred airline for corporate leaders, celebrities, and millions of Indian travellers.

But in April 2019, the airline that once ruled India’s skies suddenly stopped flying.

More than 20,000 employees lost their jobs, hundreds of flights were cancelled overnight, and Indian banks were left with thousands of crores in unpaid loans.

So what really happened?

In this business case study, we explore the rise, dominance, and dramatic collapse of Jet Airways, uncovering the real business decisions, industry changes, financial pressures, and competitive shifts that transformed India’s most admired airline into one of the biggest corporate collapses in Indian aviation history.

The Business Decisions That Changed Everything
• The high-stakes acquisition of Air Sahara

The Debt Crisis
• How rising fuel prices and heavy loans created financial strain

The Final Shutdown in 2019
• What happened on the night Jet Airways stopped flying

🌍 Why this story matters

• Case Study in Aviation Economics: Jet Airways shows how even premium airlines can struggle when the industry shifts toward low-cost models.
• Changing Airline Industry: Similar to airline collapses around the world, the story reflects how fuel prices, debt, and competition can reshape entire aviation markets.
• Cultural Moment in Indian Aviation: For millions of travellers, Jet Airways symbolized comfort, service, and prestige. Its disappearance marked the end of an era in Indian aviation history.
